channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula “foi pai que não tive”, disse Deolane em 2021
item.description: The opposition resurfaced a 2021 video in which lawyer Deolane Bezerra expressed admiration for President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, calling him the 'father I never had'. The video emerged after her arrest in May 2026 on suspicion of involvement in a money laundering scheme linked to the PCC. Flávio and Carlos Bolsonaro shared images of Bezerra with Lula, sparking political discussion.

item.title: Flávio, sobre uso de colete: “Não posso dar sopa para o azar”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-SP), a pre-candidate for the 2026 Brazilian presidency, announced he is now wearing a bulletproof vest at public events, citing fears of an attack similar to the one that struck his father, Jair Bolsonaro, in 2018. He justified the measure with the phrase: 'I can't give soup to luck,' meaning he refuses to leave his safety to chance.

item.title: Por que o impacto eleitoral da economia está diminuindo?
item.description: The electoral impact of the economy is declining due to partisan polarization, where voters' economic perceptions are strongly shaped by ideological loyalty rather than objective indicators. In 2022, two-thirds of Lula voters believed the economy had worsened, while only 10% of Bolsonaro voters agreed, demonstrating that economic evaluations are endogenous to partisan preference. This 'cheering' effect may intensify in 2026, making the economy less decisive in voting behavior than in past elections.

item.title: DPU pede anulação da ação contra Eduardo por parcialidade de Moraes
item.description: The Public Defender's Office (DPU) has requested the annulment of the case against Eduardo Bolsonaro, citing objective lack of impartiality by relator Alexandre de Moraes, who was personally affected by the investigations — including the revocation of his visa under the Magnitsky Act. The DPU, acting as Eduardo’s defense due to his lack of appointed counsel, argues his statements in the U.S. are protected by parliamentary immunity. The case stems from allegations of pressure on the Supreme Court related to the 2025 attempted coup investigation.

item.title: Quem era presidente municipal do PL que morreu após partida de futebol
item.description: Ademar Pahl Filho, known as Ademar Popeye, the municipal president of the Liberal Party (PL) in Navegantes (SC), died at age 40 after suffering a heart attack during a football match with friends. He was a businessman, digital influencer with over 27 thousand followers, a critic of President Lula’s government, and a supporter of Bolsonaro. His death was mourned by right-wing allies, including federal deputy Julia Zanatta and the PL of Santa Catarina.

item.title: Alerj rebate falas de Lula sobre “milícia organizada”
item.description: The Legislative Assembly of Rio de Janeiro (Alerj) responded to remarks by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who described the state legislature as an 'organized militia' during a Fiocruz event. In an official statement, Alerj said it respects institutions and expects the same respect from all national authorities, including the President of Brazil.

item.title: “Não posso dar sopa ao azar”, diz Flávio sobre colete à prova de balas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, pre-candidate for president and senator, said he wears a bulletproof vest because he 'can't give soup at random', referring to threats against himself and his family. He referenced the 2018 stabbing of his father, Jair Bolsonaro, and declared he is prepared to face those trying to intimidate him, without clearly identifying who 'they' are.

item.title: Fazenda Nacional cobra dívida de candidato a presidente da República
item.description: The National Treasury's Prosecutor's Office (PGFN) is pursuing a R$ 41,1 thousand tax debt linked to Martin Artefatos de Metais, a company where Renan Santos was a partner, registered in the Union's Active Debt for alleged irregular dissolution of a legal entity. The candidate denies liability, stating he joined the company in 2010 and left in October 2020, and that the debts originated in 2002/2003 under previous management. The PGFN has requested asset seizure via the Sisbajud system to recover the amount.

item.title: Flávio acena a Aldo depois de DC ameaçar tirá-lo da disputa
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro reached out to Aldo Rebelo by phone as a gesture of sympathy amid Aldo’s internal struggles within the DC after party leader João Caldas nominated Joaquim Barbosa as a presidential pre-candidate. While no vice-presidential arrangement was discussed, allies are speculating about a potential alliance. Flávio also faces backlash from a leaked audio in which he asked for money from Daniel Vorcaro, who is imprisoned, prompting allies to urge him to strengthen his campaign with policy proposals and a running mate.

item.title: A resposta dos deputados que Lula chamou de ‘milicianos’ no Rio
item.description: President Lula called Rio state deputies 'militiamen' and demanded the arrest of governors linked to organized crime, prompting the Rio Legislative Assembly (Alerj) to reject his remarks as unacceptable and demand institutional respect. Alerj President Douglas Ruas (PL) accused Lula and Eduardo Paes of lacking moral authority on security, referencing Lula’s past comments about drug traffickers. The Alerj faces an image crisis after three deputies were arrested in under a year on suspicion of ties to militias.

item.title: Censura seria um prêmio para ‘Dark Horse’
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) extended Lula's positive agenda at public expense by becoming entangled in explanations about his relationship with banker Daniel Vorcaro, a major sponsor of the film 'Dark Horse'. The collaboration between Lulists and Bolsonarists in the 2026 electoral race is described as mutually beneficial, with each side leveraging the other to boost their narratives. Censoring 'Dark Horse' would be seen as an indirect award, increasing the film's visibility and political impact.

item.title: Perfil do DC usou vídeo com IA de Joaquim Barbosa sem autorização
item.description: An Instagram profile linked to the Democracia Cristã party published an AI-generated video featuring former Supreme Court Justice Joaquim Barbosa as a presidential pre-candidate without his authorization. The video also includes manipulated images of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and President Lula, sparking internal party conflict, as Aldo Rebelo, another pre-candidate, denounced the material as an 'affront' and threatened legal action if his candidacy is blocked.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro mantém força nas redes mesmo após repercussão do caso Master
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro maintained strong social media performance after the Master case, recording 8.8 million interactions in ten days despite 65.4% of mentions being negative. His digital mobilization capacity remains high due to sharing among supporters, expanding his reach beyond the Bolsonarist base. The Bites survey also highlights Renan Santos as the second most-interacted presidential candidate with 5.6 million interactions, while Lula recorded 4 million in the same period.

item.title: Surpresa e atritos internos: os bastidores da entrada de Joaquim Barbosa na cena eleitoral
item.description: The Christian Democracy party (DC) is facing an internal crisis after its national president, João Caldas, unilaterally replaced Aldo Rebelo as the party's presidential pre-candidate with former Supreme Court Justice Joaquim Barbosa, without prior consultation. Rebelo, who had been campaigning for four months, refused to step down and threatened legal action, while state leaders like Paulo Cesar Quartiero of Roraima and Cândido Vaccarezza of São Paulo denounced Barbosa as a 'leftist' and 'traitor', blocking him from party channels and withdrawing their own local candidacies. The national executive has opened expulsion proceedings against Rebelo, but the deep split threatens to destroy the party's viability in the 2026 elections.

item.title: Moraes suspende julgamento sobre anistia a partidos que descumpriram cota racial
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes requested a view and suspended the STF's judgment on the amnesty for parties that failed to comply with the racial quota for resources allocated to women and Black candidates in the 2022 elections. The suspension may last up to 90 days, while the prior vote showed a majority in favor of the amnesty, with Cristiano Zanin, Dias Toffoli, André Mendonça, Nunes Marques, Luiz Fux and Gilmar Mendes supporting it, and Flávio Dino, Cármen Lúcia and Edson Fachin opposing it.

item.title: Pesquisa identifica 32 candidaturas outsiders no Brasil de 2002 a 2022
item.description: A ReDem study identified 32 presidential outsider candidacies in Brazil from 2002 to 2022, revealing that these candidates, often portrayed as signs of systemic crisis, actually follow a historical pattern of situational fluctuations rather than a permanent upward trend. The analysis warns against misinterpreting isolated spikes as evidence of structural breakdown, noting that the phenomenon fits the logic of 'pulp politics' — where electoral contests are framed as moral battles between corrupt villains and heroic saviors, turning routine politics into extraordinary narratives of salvation.

item.title: Gilmar vota por manter escolas cívico-militares em SP com restrições
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes voted to uphold the constitutionality of São Paulo's Civic-Military School Program but imposed significant restrictions, banning extremist militaristic activities, requiring uniforms to respect cultural and religious diversity, keeping pedagogical and administrative management under civilian responsibility, and declaring unconstitutional the payment of military police in schools. The virtual trial took place from May 22 to May 29, 2026, with PSOL and PT as plaintiffs, arguing the program violates the LDB and exceeds state authority. The law, enacted in May 2024, was a campaign promise of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas.

item.title: José de Abreu faz 80 anos entre papéis marcantes e polêmicas públicas
item.description: José de Abreu, an 80-year-old Brazilian actor with over 50 years of career, is known for memorable roles on Globo such as Chico in Ti-Ti-Ti, Carlos Lacerda in JK, and Nilo in Avenida Brasil. Beyond his artistic trajectory, he has become a polarizing public figure due to ideological stances on social media, public clashes with colleagues like Maria Zilda and Murilo Rosa, and his announcement as a federal deputy candidate for the PT in the 2026 elections, endorsed by Maricá's mayor Washington Quaquá.

item.title: Os candidatos a ‘Dark Horse’ na eleição presidencial de 2026
item.description: The article discusses dark horse candidates in Brazil's 2026 presidential election, highlighting Renan Santos of the Missão party, who polls at 6.9% nationally and leads among voters aged 16–24 with 36.1%. It also mentions Joaquim Barbosa, former STF justice, as a potential candidate for the Democracia Cristã party, emphasizing anti-corruption as a central theme amid scandals involving Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Pesquisas eleitorais: como está a disputa Lula x Flávio após novos Datafolha e AtlasIntel
item.description: The AtlasIntel and Datafolha polls released after the scandal involving Flávio Bolsonaro and Banco Master showed a significant increase in Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's lead over Flávio Bolsonaro. In the first round, Lula leads with 47% (AtlasIntel) and 40% (Datafolha), while Flávio dropped to 34.3% and 31%, respectively. The scandal also generated widespread public awareness, with over 90% of voters aware of the audio and a notable rise in associating the scandal with Jair Bolsonaro's circle.

item.title: A parceria de Nunes Marques e André Mendonça no comando do TSE
item.description: TSE President Minister Nunes Marques is innovating by sharing court management with Vice President Minister André Mendonça, rather than leading the Electoral Justice alone as past presidents did. He aims to have Mendonça actively involved in the frontline preparations for the 2026 elections, including reviewing irregular propaganda cases previously handled by Minister Estela Aranha. This partnership was highlighted in public events, such as an FSB Group’s Seta event on AI in elections, to demonstrate unity and consistency in leadership.

item.title: Michelle jogando à la Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro is adopting a passive political stance, similar to what Flávio Bolsonaro did from December until mid-January. While Flávio has already resumed public activities, Michelle remains silent, sparking speculation about her electoral strategy for 2026. This shift in focus among Bolsonaro family members suggests a potential realignment of roles in the upcoming campaign.

item.title: Com holofotes em Vorcaro e nos Bolsonaros, Congresso deu rasteira no povo
item.description: While the country was fixated on the scandal involving Flávio Bolsonaro and his request for R$ 134 million from banker Daniel Vorcaro, Congress took advantage of the distraction to pass harmful measures without transparency or proper debate. The article criticizes the Legislative's opportunistic behavior, acting behind the scenes when public attention is focused on high-impact media controversies. The phrase 'passed the herd' symbolizes the silent approval of proposals contrary to the people's interests.

item.title: Haddad defendia “taxa das blusinhas” com convicção, diz Lula
item.description: President Lula stated that former Finance Minister Fernando Haddad defended the 'blusinhas tax' with conviction, a measure abolished by the federal government this month due to political backlash and widespread public rejection. Lula added that Haddad viewed the tax as a way to protect domestic industry from unfair competition by low-cost imported goods.

item.title: Sindmagis pede a Lula que vaga de Barroso no STF seja ocupada por magistrado de carreira
item.description: The Brazilian Magistrates' Union (Sindmagis) urged President Lula to fill the STF vacancy left by Justice Luís Roberto Barroso's retirement with a career magistrate, proposing a triple list selected by the national judiciary. The group argues this would enhance institutional representation and ensure rulings are more aligned with the realities of the justice system.

item.title: Incertezas e atritos marcam os bastidores do novo voo eleitoral de Joaquim Barbosa
item.description: Former Supreme Court Justice Joaquim Barbosa was announced as the presidential candidate of the Christian Democracy party, sparking internal conflict as Aldo Rebelo, who already had a secured pre-candidacy, denounced the move as unilateral and threatened legal action. State leaders of the party labeled Barbosa an opportunistic leftist, incompatible with the party’s nationalist and pro-Amazon stance, leading to withdrawn local candidacies and an expulsion process against Rebelo.

item.title: Lula mantém vantagem sobre Flávio entre eleitores de centro, diz Datafolha
item.description: Lula maintains an advantage over Flávio Bolsonaro among center voters, according to the latest Datafolha poll. The president has 29% voting intention in this group, compared to 20% for Bolsonaro's son. The center is defined on a 1 to 7 ideological scale.

item.title: Os eventos de junho desmarcados com Flávio Bolsonaro na Faria Lima
item.description: Events scheduled for June at Faria Lima, featuring Flávio Bolsonaro, were canceled or postponed over the past ten days. The move was described as prudent amid a sensitive political climate. The full article is available only to subscribers.

item.title: Lula mencionou “vontade grande” de ajudar o RJ, diz governador
item.description: Rio de Janeiro's interim governor, Ricardo Couto, said President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva expressed a 'great willingness' to help the state during meetings on May 22 and 23, 2026. Lula publicly praised Couto at the inauguration of Fiocruz's Technological Development Center in Health, but also made controversial remarks suggesting that if the state legislature chose the governor, 'it would be a militiaman,' and called for imprisoning 'thieves who governed the state' and lawmakers tied to militias. His comments drew criticism from lawmakers like Sóstenes Cavalcante (PL-RJ), who accused the president of undermining democracy.

item.title: Governador interino do RJ decide desapropriar terreno da Refit e licitar área para outras empresas
item.description: Rio de Janeiro's interim governor, Ricardo Magro, is set to expropriate the land where the Refit refinery operates — described by Lula as the 'crown jewel' of the country's largest public debtor. The move aims to auction the area to other companies amid allegations of widespread tax evasion. The report is exclusive to subscribers, requiring registration for full access.

item.title: Estadão inicia ‘Brasil Adiante’, ciclo de debates para apresentar propostas concretas ao País
item.description: Estadão has launched 'Brasil Adiante', a series of debates running until August to develop concrete proposals on health, education, security, and institutions, aiming to deliver an actionable agenda for the first 24 months of the next government. The first event, held on May 27 at Espaço JK Eventos, focused on Institutional Stability and Growth Foundations, featuring panelists like Marcos Mendes, Jéssika Moreira, and Pedro Parente, moderated by Álvaro Gribel. The resulting document will be presented to the winner of the 2026 presidential election in November.

item.title: Fantasmas do passado
item.description: The article argues that governments, including Lula's, use public resources to stay in power, a practice criticized as 'making deals with the devil,' as admitted by Dilma Rousseff. It emphasizes that re-election is widely contested due to this behavior and that legislative elections are more influenced by regional political machines than by national loyalty. The content is exclusive to subscribers.

item.title: Brasil propõe pacto contra feminicídio ao Mercosul para combater violência contra as mulheres
item.description: The Brazilian government proposed a regional Mercosul pact to combat femicide, aiming for joint prevention, protection, and justice access actions, with initial support from Uruguay and ongoing analysis in Argentina. The meeting also highlighted national measures to increase digital platform accountability for online violence against women, including mandatory removal of harmful content within two hours and algorithmic adjustments to curb coordinated attacks.

item.title: Cortes de vídeo viram mercado e arma de guerra para as eleições
item.description: Video cuts, popularized by Pablo Marçal in 2024, have become a strategic tool in Brazil's 2026 elections, with platforms and AI tools like Real Oficial accelerating their production. Although the Superior Electoral Court banned 'cut tournaments' to prevent undue influence, the practice remains relevant in the digital war for voter attention. Experts emphasize that success depends on the volume and engagement generated by these viral snippets.

item.title: Tarcísio e Haddad montam coalizões ao governo paulista e reduzem opções nas urnas
item.description: The 2026 São Paulo gubernatorial election is shaping up to be a polarized contest between Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) and Fernando Haddad (PT), each building broad coalitions across the political spectrum. Tarcísio has secured backing from PL, PSD, PP, União Brasil, MDB, Podemos and Novo, while Haddad relies on PSB, PSOL, Rede and PDT, aligned with Lula’s national base. Alternative candidates such as Paulo Serra (PSDB) and Kim Kataguiri (Missão) aim to break the polarization but struggle to gain traction due to limited grassroots reach and insufficient party support.

item.title: SP: Kim Kataguiri e Paulo Serra querem coligação e piso nas pesquisas para confirmar candidaturas ao governo
item.description: Former Santo André mayor Paulo Serra (PSDB) and federal deputy Kim Kataguiri (Missão) have conditioned their candidacies for São Paulo governor on forming coalitions with at least two representative parties beyond Cidadania, aiming to boost free airtime and grassroots campaign reach. Both trail with 5% in recent Quaest polls behind Tarcísio de Freitas (38%) and Fernando Haddad (26%), and view electoral viability as a prerequisite to proceed, with Serra negotiating in Brasília to secure support from up to 300 state deputies.

item.title: Estilos opostos e visões de mundo distintas moldam marqueteiros dos presidenciáveis
item.description: The change in Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign communications team, with Marcello Lopes departing and Eduardo Fischer joining, reflects an effort to stabilize the senator’s image following a scandal tied to his association with Banco Master’s owner. Fischer, known for beer advertising and with limited political experience, must adapt traditional marketing strategies to a shortened, highly polarized electoral cycle dominated by social media influence. The recent Datafolha poll shows a decline in Bolsonaro’s voting intentions, dropping in both first and second round scenarios against Lula, underscoring the political cost of the controversy.

item.title: Datafolha: maioria condena pedido de dinheiro de Flávio a Vorcaro, mas 88% de seus eleitores ainda o querem na disputa
item.description: Despite 64% of voters deeming Flávio Bolsonaro's request for money from Daniel Vorcaro to fund a biopic of Jair Bolsonaro inappropriate, 88% of his base still supports him in the 2026 presidential race. The Datafolha poll shows the scandal reduced his lead over Lula and increased his rejection, but loyalty among his voters remains strong, with 73% saying their trust in him has not changed.

item.title: Aprovação de projeto que prevê benefícios a partidos teve discursos de apenas quatro deputados e uniu governo e oposição
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved a bill granting benefits to political parties, including mass messaging during elections, in a session marked by low attendance and minimal debate. Only four deputies spoke, all criticizing the proposal, while rapporteur Rodrigo Gambale defended it, claiming it had been negotiated for months. The vote was conducted symbolically without a nominal record, after leaders agreed to consider urgency and merit on the same day to avoid political backlash.

item.title: Mesmo preso, Bolsonaro conduz direita que não quis se endireitar
item.description: Even while imprisoned, Jair Bolsonaro continues to exert influence over the Brazilian right, exploiting what the text frames as the cowardice of leaders like Tarcísio de Freitas and Ronaldo Caiado, who have not directly challenged him. His leadership persists due to others' inaction, not his own strength.

item.title: Lula não encontra limite em sua gastança eleitoreira
item.description: The Lula government has intensified the distribution of social benefits and programs with a clear electoral aim, seeking to boost the president's popularity ahead of the 2026 elections. While such spending increases are common before elections, the initiative is described as lacking limits and excessively frenetic, drawing criticism for using public funds for partisan purposes. The article notes that full access requires a subscription.

item.title: Livro mostra transformações do Brasil em 20 anos de eleições presidenciais
item.description: The book 'O país dividido' by political scientist Jairo Nicolau analyzes how Brazil changed between the 2002 and 2022 presidential elections, highlighting the social, economic, and political transformations that led to a more polarized electorate. The work shows that the Brazil that elected Lula in 2022 was significantly different from the one that elected him in 2002, reflecting profound societal changes.

item.title: 'Casa Branca tentará interferir na eleição brasileira', diz escritora Anne Applebaum
item.description: American writer and historian Anne Applebaum warned that the White House will attempt to interfere in Brazil's 2026 election, highlighting a global pattern of democratic backsliding in which authoritarian powers weaponize the judiciary to suppress opposition and enrich allies. Applebaum, a Pulitzer Prize winner, links this trend to the strategic use of legal institutions by autocratic leaders, citing historical and contemporary examples.

item.title: "Lula não tem moral para dar lição sobre combate ao crime", diz Ruas
item.description: The president of the Rio de Janeiro Legislative Assembly, Douglas Ruas (PL), criticized President Lula for suggesting that Rio would have a governor linked to militias if the Assembly indicated the next candidate, stating that Lula 'has no moral authority to lecture' on crime fighting. Ruas argued that during PT governments, criminal factions and militias grew, citing Bahia and Ceará as violent states governed by the party. He also accused Eduardo Paes (PSD), Lula's ally, of allowing militias to advance in Rio during his tenure as mayor.

item.title: Não é possível homens maus estarem no controle do país, diz Malafaia
item.description: Pastor Silas Malafaia criticized the presence of 'evil men' in power during the 2026 March for Jesus in Rio de Janeiro, stating Christians should not vote for those supporting abortion, gender ideology, or persecuting Christians abroad. He praised Rio state legislator Douglas Ruas (PL) as representing all branches of government and lamented the absence of pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), who canceled his participation.

item.title: Áudio entre Flávio e Vorcaro abalou confiança do mercado, dizem empresários
item.description: Audio recordings between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and former banker Daniel Vorcaro have raised concerns among business leaders, who say they have undermined market confidence in the pre-campaign of the former president’s son. The conversations, released this month, raise questions about influence and transparency in the political-economic sphere.

item.title: Sóstenes critica fala de Lula que associou Alerj a milicianos
item.description: PL chamber leader Sóstenes Cavalcante criticized President Lula’s remarks linking the Alerj to militias, stating that all state deputies were elected by vote and that Lula attacked the institution, voters, and democracy. He expressed solidarity with Alerj members, especially president Douglas Ruas, noting that interim governor Ricardo Couto assumed office after legal resignations and removals of figures like Cláudio Castro and Rodrigo Bacellar, both barred from office until 2030.

item.title: Pesquisas e arquitetura da destruição. Sempre foi difícil Lula perder
item.description: The article criticizes the Bolsonarist narrative that downplays Lula's lead in polls, noting that despite recent fluctuations, the former president remains the favorite to defeat Flávio Bolsonaro in a potential runoff. The author dismisses claims of Lula's significant decline, comparing Flávio's supporters to the Flavian emperors who built the Colosseum — a symbol of ruin and spectacle. He argues that Bolsonarists are on a self-destructive path, while affirming his support for Lula and distancing himself from the far-right.

item.title: Governo Lula prepara ofensiva com estados contra roubo de celulares
item.description: The Lula government is expanding the Celular Seguro program to combat phone theft and robbery, focusing on integrating state systems, accelerating investigations, and holding criminals and resale networks accountable. The initiative includes implementing the National Base of Restricted Cellphones (BNCR), which will consolidate theft reports, device identifiers, and owner records, and will be shared with police and state public security secretariats.

item.title: Sem Flávio, Marcha para Jesus no RJ teve discurso político de Malafaia
item.description: Evangelical leader Silas Malafaia, aligned with Bolsonarism, delivered a political speech at the 19th March for Jesus in Rio de Janeiro, linking electoral decisions to religious values and criticizing Christians who, he claims, do not apply their faith in politics, saying they 'vote for crooks' or 'thieves'. He also accused 'evil men' of controlling the nation, citing supporters of abortion, gender ideology, and 'moral depravity'. The event saw the notable absence of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a presidential pre-candidate, who canceled his appearance to stay in Brasília for meetings with his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro.
